title: Necromunda — Meaning, Genes, And Nothing Else #Shorts
description:
What looks like free choice in Necromunda is older than choice itself. Necromunda is a skirmish tabletop war game originally produced by Games Workshop in 1995. In Necromunda, players control rival gangs battling each other in the Underhive, a place of anarchy and violence in the depths below the hive city.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. When a group of slaves escapes, they already have weapons to help them survive along with experience gained in gladiator-style combat they are often pressed into. From a player perspective, Pit Slaves are all experienced and expensive, having no cannon fodder.

scenes.narration: What looks like free choice in Necromunda is older than choice itself. Necromunda is a skirmish tabletop war
game originally produced by Games Workshop in 1995. In Necromunda, players control rival gangs battling each other in
the Underhive, a place of anarchy and violence in the depths below the hive city. Nobody designed the
part of Necromunda you experience — it was inherited. As in its parent game Warhammer 40,000, Necromunda uses
28 mm miniatures (approximately 1:56) and terrain (in this case, the Underhive – a heavily polluted, underground industrial
environment). Necromunda allows players to develop their gangs between battles, gaining experience, gaining and losing new members or
equipment, according to a set of rules.
